description: This test validates the exception handling behavior when querying the initialization status of a non-existent child initializer in a multi-threaded background initialization system. The test examines the MultiBackgroundInitializerResults class and its isException method, asserting that a NoSuchElementException is thrown when an unknown initializer name is provided. Initialize the test by calling the helper method checkInitialize which sets up a MultiBackgroundInitializer with five child background initializers using names constructed from the CHILD_INIT constant plus an index, starts the initialization process, retrieves the MultiBackgroundInitializerResults object, and validates that all child initializers completed successfully without exceptions. After the helper method returns the results object, invoke the isException method on the MultiBackgroundInitializerResults instance with the string literal "unknown" as the parameter, which represents a non-existent initializer name. Assert that this method call throws a NoSuchElementException using the assertThrows assertion, validating that the system properly handles requests for status information about initializers that were never registered with the MultiBackgroundInitializer. The isException method internally calls checkName to validate the provided name exists in the initializers map, and when the name is not found, checkName throws the NoSuchElementException as expected. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

Advance the iterator to the next element, then attempt to remove that element from the underlying collection through the iterator's remove method. description: This test validates that an object pool's automatic eviction mechanism properly removes idle objects over time according to configured parameters. Initialize a pool with a factory and configure it to hold up to 500 objects with eviction settings that remove 100 objects per eviction run, mark objects for eviction after a short idle duration, run eviction checks every 500 milliseconds, and validate objects while idle. Borrow 500 objects from the pool and immediately return them all to create a full set of idle objects. Wait for the eviction process to run and assert that the number of idle objects progressively decreases below specific thresholds as time passes, eventually reaching zero idle objects. Repeat the entire borrowing and returning cycle a second time to verify that the eviction behavior remains consistent across multiple uses. Throughout the process, verify that the pool correctly reduces its idle count at each checkpoint, confirming that the eviction timer and validation mechanisms work as expected. After completion, clean up the pool resources and verify that no management beans remain registered and that the eviction timer has been properly shut down. This test uses JUnit for assertions and timeout management.

This test validates the hour-of-day rounding functionality of the DateUtils utility class, specifically testing that dates are correctly rounded to the nearest hour boundary when using the Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY field. Initialize a DateFormat field of the test class as a SimpleDateFormat with pattern "MMM dd, yyyy H:mm:ss.SSS" and English locale, then parse multiple Date fields including targetHourOfDayDate set to "June 1, 2008 8:00:00.000" and januaryOneDate set to "January 1, 2008 0:00:00.000", along with a Calendar field januaryOneCalendar configured with the januaryOneDate time. Set the calendar field constant to Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY, then parse roundedUpDate to "June 1, 2008 9:00:00.000", assign roundedDownDate to the existing targetHourOfDayDate, and parse lastRoundedDownDate to "June 1, 2008 8:29:59.999". Call the helper method baseRoundTest with these dates and the calendar field, which internally tests DateUtils.round method behavior by adding one millisecond to the last round down date to create a first round up date, then asserting equality between expected rounded dates and actual results from DateUtils.round for both Date objects, Calendar objects, and generic Object parameters, validating that dates round down when closer to the lower boundary and round up when closer to the upper boundary. Parse minDate to "December 31, 2007 23:30:00.000" and maxDate to "January 1, 2008 0:29:59.999", then call the helper method roundToJanuaryFirst with these dates and the calendar field, which verifies that dates within the rounding range of January 1st correctly round to januaryOneDate and januaryOneCalendar, while dates outside this range by one millisecond do not equal the January 1st targets, using assertEquals for positive cases and assertNotEquals for boundary validation cases. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the hour-of-day rounding functionality of a date utility component by initializing a date formatter with English locale and creating various target dates representing different time scenarios including January 1st 2007, June 1st 2008 at different hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds, along with a January 1st 2008 reference date and corresponding calendar instance. Set the calendar field to represent hour-of-day and define expected rounded dates including a rounded-up date at 9:00 AM, a rounded-down date at 8:00 AM, and a last rounded-down date at 8:29:59.999 AM on June 1st 2008. Call the base round test helper which exercises the date utility's round method with both Date and Calendar objects, asserting that dates round correctly to the nearest hour boundary by comparing the results against expected rounded-up and rounded-down values, and also testing the round method when passed as generic objects. Additionally, define minimum and maximum dates around December 31st 2007 and January 1st 2008 to test edge cases, then call the January first rounding helper which validates that dates within the rounding boundary correctly round to January 1st 2008, while dates outside the boundary do not, using both Date and Calendar representations and asserting equality for valid cases and inequality for boundary violations. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that client wait time statistics are accurately tracked when borrowing objects from a keyed pool with artificial creation latency. Initialize a factory with a creation delay of 200 milliseconds to simulate slow object creation, then create a keyed object pool using this factory with default configuration. Borrow an object using a specific key, which will trigger object creation and introduce the configured latency, then verify that both the maximum and mean borrow wait times are at least 100 milliseconds to account for the creation delay with some tolerance for timing variations. Return the borrowed object to the pool, then immediately borrow another object with the same key, which should retrieve the existing object without creation delay. Assert that the maximum borrow wait time remains above 100 milliseconds from the first borrow, while the mean borrow wait time should be less than 200 milliseconds but greater than 20 milliseconds, reflecting the average of the slow first borrow and the fast second borrow. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the eviction behavior of a generic object pool by configuring eviction parameters and observing how idle objects are progressively removed over time. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool during setup, then configure the pool with a maximum of 500 idle and total objects, 100 tests per eviction run, a minimum evictable idle duration of 250 milliseconds, eviction runs every 500 milliseconds, and enable testing while idle. Borrow 500 objects from the pool using an array to track active objects, then return all 500 objects back to the pool to make them idle. Sleep for 1000 milliseconds and assert that the number of idle objects is less than 500, then continue sleeping for 600 millisecond intervals while asserting that the idle count progressively decreases below 400, 300, 200, and 100 objects, finally reaching exactly zero idle objects. Repeat the entire borrowing and returning cycle with the same 500 objects, followed by the same series of sleep intervals and assertions to verify consistent eviction behavior across multiple cycles. During teardown, clear and close the object pool, unregister any remaining MBeans from the platform MBean server, assert that no pools remain registered, and verify that the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses the JUnit framework with a timeout annotation set to 60 seconds.

This test validates that the pool correctly handles concurrent access scenarios when validation failures occur during object invalidation without throwing null pointer exceptions. Initialize a pool with a simple factory, configure it to have a maximum of one total object, enable validation on object creation, and set the maximum wait time to indefinite. Initialize a failing factory that can simulate various failure conditions and create an empty keyed pool using this factory, skipping the test if pool creation is not supported. Set up method call tracking to monitor factory interactions and borrow an object from the pool using a specific key. Clear the tracking records and invalidate the borrowed object, then verify that the factory's destroy method was called with the correct key and object parameters. Reset the pool state and borrow a second object, then configure the factory to fail during object destruction. Attempt to invalidate this second object and assert that the expected private exception is thrown to confirm that destruction failures propagate correctly. Allow a brief delay for any deferred operations to complete, remove any destroy method calls from the tracking records, and verify that no unexpected method calls occurred during the failure scenario. Finally, close the pool to complete the test and perform cleanup by nullifying the pool reference. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the string substitution functionality of a string substitutor component by exercising its ability to replace variable placeholders with corresponding values from a lookup map. Initialize a hash map containing key-value pairs representing substitution variables, such as mapping "animal" to "quick brown fox" and "target" to "lazy dog". Create a string substitutor instance using this value map, then test its replacement capabilities by providing a template string containing placeholder variables in the format "${variable_name}" that should be substituted with "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." Call the helper method with the expected result, the template string, and a boolean flag indicating substring testing should be performed. The helper method creates multiple representations of the template string including character arrays, string buffers, string builders, and custom string builder objects, then invokes various replace methods on each representation to verify consistent substitution behavior. Assert that each replacement operation produces the expected fully substituted string, and when substring testing is enabled, verify that partial replacements within specified character ranges also work correctly. Additionally, test in-place replacement methods that modify the original string objects directly, asserting that these operations return true to indicate successful replacement and that the modified objects contain the expected substituted content. Clean up by nullifying the values map after test completion. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize three IllegalArgumentException assertions using assertThrows to verify that the erodingPool method rejects null KeyedObjectPool instances and non-positive erosion factors with appropriate error messages. Create an ArrayList called calledMethods to track method invocations and instantiate a MethodCallLogger InvocationHandler that overrides the invoke method to log all method calls while returning Integer value 1 for any Integer return types to simulate non-zero pool statistics. description: This test validates that an object pool serves waiting threads in a fair, first-come-first-served order when fairness is enabled. Initialize a pool configuration with fairness enabled, last-in-first-out disabled, and maximum capacity set to accommodate all test objects. Create a pool using this configuration and a simple factory. Exhaust the pool by borrowing all available objects and storing them. Launch multiple threads that will each attempt to borrow an object, introducing small delays between thread starts to establish a clear ordering. Return all borrowed objects back to the pool, which should trigger the waiting threads to receive objects in the same order they began waiting. Monitor all threads until they complete their borrowing operations, verifying that none encounter errors during execution. The test uses JUnit 5 framework with timeout constraints.

This test validates the basic string substitution functionality of the StrSubstitutor class by verifying that variable placeholders in templates are correctly replaced with their corresponding values from a lookup map. The test specifically examines the replace and replaceIn methods across multiple string-like data types including String, char array, StringBuffer, StringBuilder, StrBuilder, and MutableObject, ensuring that both full string replacement and substring replacement operations produce the expected results. Initialize a HashMap field of the test class with key-value pairs where "animal" maps to "quick brown fox" and "target" maps to "lazy dog" during setup. Call the helper method doTestReplace with three arguments: the expected result string "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.", a template string containing variable placeholders "The ${animal} jumps over the ${target}.", and a boolean value true to enable substring testing. Within the helper method, create a shortened version of the expected result by removing the first and last characters, then instantiate a new StrSubstitutor object with the values map. Execute the replace method on the StrSubstitutor instance using the template string and assert that the result equals the expected full string, then perform substring replacement by calling replace with start index 1 and end index of template length minus 2, asserting the result equals the shortened expected string. Convert the template to a character array and repeat the same replacement operations, asserting both full and substring results match expectations. Create StringBuffer, StringBuilder, StrBuilder, and MutableObject instances initialized with the template string, then call replace on each, asserting the results equal the expected string for full replacement and the shortened string for substring operations. Execute replaceIn methods on new StringBuffer, StringBuilder, and StrBuilder instances, asserting that each method returns true indicating successful replacement and that the toString output of each modified object equals the expected result string, with substring operations performed using start and end indices that modify only the specified portion while leaving the remainder untouched. Clean up by setting the values field to null during teardown. This test uses JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the fairness behavior of a generic object pool when multiple threads compete for borrowed objects. Initialize a simple factory and create a generic object pool configuration with a maximum total of 40 objects, maximum idle of 40, fairness enabled, and LIFO disabled, then construct a new generic object pool using the factory and configuration. Exhaust the pool by borrowing all 40 available objects and storing them in an array. Create and start 40 test threads that will each attempt to borrow one object with a 2-second timeout, introducing a 10-millisecond delay between thread starts to ensure they begin in the correct order. Return all borrowed objects back to the pool one by one, which should allow the waiting threads to acquire objects in the order they were started due to the fairness setting. Wait for all threads to complete their execution, checking each thread's completion status in a loop with 500-millisecond intervals. Assert that no threads failed during execution by examining each thread's failure status and error information. During teardown, clear and close the object pool, unregister any remaining MBean instances from the platform MBean server, assert that no pools remain registered, and verify that the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 with timeout annotations and warning suppressions for raw types.

This test validates the proper behavior of keyed object pool invalidation operations, specifically ensuring that invalidated objects are correctly destroyed and that destroy operation exceptions are properly propagated to callers. Initialize a FailingKeyedPooledObjectFactory instance and create an empty KeyedObjectPool using the makeEmptyPool helper method, catching any UnsupportedOperationException and returning early if the test is not supported by the implementation. Create an ArrayList of MethodCall objects to track expected factory method invocations. Borrow an object from the pool using borrowObject with a KEY parameter, then call the clear helper method to reset both the factory's method call tracking and the expected methods list. Invoke invalidateObject on the pool with the KEY and borrowed object, then add a new MethodCall with destroyObject method name, KEY, and the object to the expected methods list, and assert that the factory's getMethodCalls matches the expected methods using assertEquals to verify the object was properly destroyed. Call the reset helper method which clears the pool, resets factory method tracking, and resets factory failure flags. Borrow a second object from the pool using borrowObject with KEY, clear the method tracking again, then configure the factory to fail on destroy operations by calling setDestroyObjectFail with true. Use assertThrows to verify that calling invalidateObject with KEY and the second object throws a PrivateException with the message "Expecting destroy exception to propagate", confirming that destroy failures are properly communicated to the caller. Sleep for 250 milliseconds to allow for any deferred operations, then call AbstractTestObjectPool.removeDestroyObjectCall on the factory's method calls to handle potential deferred destroy calls, and assert that the remaining method calls match the expected empty list. Finally, close the pool and in the tearDown method, set the pool field to null for cleanup. This test uses the Test annotation and employs JUnit testing framework for assertions and exception validation.

This test validates the invalidation behavior of a keyed object pool by creating a failing keyed pooled object factory and initializing an empty pool with it, skipping the test if the pool implementation doesn't support the operation. Initialize a method call tracking list to monitor factory interactions, then borrow an object from the pool using a key and clear the factory's recorded method calls. Call the pool's invalidate object method with the key and borrowed object, then verify that the factory's destroy object method was invoked by asserting the expected method call sequence matches the actual calls recorded. Reset the pool and factory state, borrow a second object, clear the method tracking again, and configure the factory to fail during object destruction. Attempt to invalidate the second object and assert that a PrivateException is thrown with an appropriate error message, then pause execution briefly to allow for any deferred operations. Remove any destroy object calls from the recorded method calls and verify the expected method sequence still matches the factory's actual calls, finally closing the pool and cleaning up by setting the pool reference to null in teardown. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the fairness behavior of object borrowing from a GenericObjectPool when multiple threads are competing for pooled objects, ensuring that threads are served in the order they request objects rather than in a last-in-first-out manner. The test exercises the GenericObjectPool's fairness configuration by creating multiple concurrent threads that attempt to borrow objects from an exhausted pool, then validates that these threads receive objects in the correct chronological order when objects become available. Initialize a SimpleFactory instance and create a GenericObjectPoolConfig with maxTotal set to 40, maxIdle set to 40, fairness set to true, and lifo set to false, then construct a new GenericObjectPool using the SimpleFactory and this configuration. Exhaust the pool by borrowing all 40 available objects using the borrowObject method and storing them in a String array. Create 40 TestThread instances, each configured to borrow 1 object with a 0 delay, 2000 millisecond timeout, non-failing behavior, and a thread identifier based on the modulo of the thread index and maxTotal value, then start each thread with a 10 millisecond sleep delay between starts to ensure proper ordering. Return all borrowed objects to the pool using the returnObject method in sequential order, which should allow the waiting threads to acquire objects in the order they were started. Wait for all threads to complete by checking the complete method on each TestThread instance using Waiter.sleepQuietly with 500 millisecond intervals, and assert that no thread failed by checking the failed method and calling fail with the thread index and error message if any thread encountered an error. The test uses JUnit 5 framework with Test, Timeout, and SuppressWarnings annotations, setting a 60-second timeout limit for the entire test execution.

This test validates that a pooled object correctly calculates its idle duration immediately after creation without returning negative or zero values. Create a new pooled object wrapper containing an arbitrary object, then introduce a brief delay to ensure measurable time has passed since creation. Verify that the idle duration calculation returns a positive, non-negative value by asserting it is neither negative nor zero. Additionally, confirm that the idle duration does not exceed the active duration, as both should be equivalent to the time elapsed since creation in the initial state where no borrowing or returning has occurred. This test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates that a pooled object correctly calculates its idle duration in its initial state immediately after creation, ensuring the duration calculations are non-negative and logically consistent with the active duration. Initialize a DefaultPooledObject instance wrapping a new Object, then introduce a deliberate delay by calling Thread sleep for 200 milliseconds to ensure sufficient time has passed for meaningful duration calculations and to verify that negative time values are not returned. After the sleep period, call the getIdleDuration method on the DefaultPooledObject instance and assert that the returned Duration is not negative using assertFalse with the isNegative method, then assert that the idle duration is not zero using assertFalse with the isZero method to confirm that measurable time has elapsed since object creation. Finally, call both getIdleDuration and getActiveDuration methods and assert using assertTrue that the idle duration is less than or equal to the active duration by comparing their values with the compareTo method, where this relationship should hold true in the initial state since both durations are calculated from the creation instant to the current time, with the comment noting that less-than-or-equal comparison is used instead of equality because the "now" timestamp may differ between the two method evaluations. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that a proxied object pool correctly prevents access to returned objects by throwing exceptions when methods are called on them after return. Create a proxied object pool using a helper method, then borrow a test object from the pool and assert it is not null. Set the object's data property to a test value and verify the data can be retrieved correctly to confirm the proxied methods work while the object is borrowed. Return the object to the pool, then assert the object reference itself is still not null but verify that calling the data getter method on the returned object throws an IllegalStateException, demonstrating that the proxy prevents further use of objects after they have been returned to the pool. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

description: This test validates the interaction between object pool eviction and concurrent borrowing operations when the pool is configured with minimum idle objects. Initialize a simple factory with a make latency of 300 milliseconds and set both the factory and generic object pool maximum total to 2 objects, then configure the pool with a minimum idle count of 1. Borrow one object from the pool to establish an active object state, leaving the pool with 1 active and 0 idle objects. Create a test thread configured to perform 1 borrow operation with a 150 millisecond delay, then start this thread in parallel. Configure the pool's eviction timer to run after 100 milliseconds, which will trigger the creation of idle instances to meet the minimum idle requirement. Wait for the borrower thread to complete execution, then assert that the borrower thread did not fail during its operation. The test uses a timeout annotation with a 60-second limit and employs JUnit testing framework.

description: This test validates that string substitution functionality correctly handles empty placeholder keys and default value syntax within template strings. Initialize a mapping of replacement values containing animal and target entries, then execute substitution operations on templates that include empty placeholder braces and default value syntax with colons. The test exercises two specific scenarios: one with completely empty placeholder braces that should remain unchanged, and another using default value syntax where the placeholder should fall back to a predefined value when the key is not found. For each scenario, perform string replacement operations across multiple data types including strings, character arrays, string buffers, string builders, and custom string building utilities, validating both full string replacement and substring replacement within specified boundaries. Assert that the substitution correctly preserves empty placeholders as literal text while properly resolving default values, and verify that in-place replacement operations return true to indicate successful modifications. Clean up the mapping after test completion. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the interaction between object eviction and concurrent borrowing operations in a GenericObjectPool to ensure that eviction processes can successfully add idle objects while borrowing operations are in progress. The test configures a SimpleFactory with a make latency of 300 milliseconds and sets both the factory and GenericObjectPool maximum total to 2, while setting the pool's minimum idle to 1, then borrows one object to establish an initial state of one active and zero idle objects. Initialize a TestThread with the generic object pool, configured to run once with a 150 millisecond fixed delay before attempting to borrow, and create a Thread instance from this TestThread. Configure the generic object pool to run eviction with a duration between eviction runs of 100 milliseconds, which will trigger the evictor to create an idle instance. Start the borrower thread to initiate the concurrent borrowing operation, then call join on the borrower thread to wait for its completion. Assert that the borrower thread did not fail by calling the failed method on the TestThread and verifying it returns false, which validates that the eviction process successfully added objects without interfering with the concurrent borrowing operation. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with a timeout annotation set to 60000 milliseconds.

description: This test validates the timing behavior of a pooled object within a generic object pool by examining how borrow and return operations affect various time-related metrics. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool during setup, then borrow a string object from the pool and retrieve its corresponding pooled object wrapper. Capture the initial timing state by recording the last borrow instant, last return instant, and last used instant, then assert that the creation instant precedes or equals each of these timestamps. Introduce a 200-millisecond delay to ensure measurable time differences, then verify that the active duration is neither negative nor zero and that various duration comparisons hold true, including that the active duration is less than or equal to the idle duration. Assert that the current timing values are greater than or equal to the initially captured values, indicating proper timestamp progression. Return the borrowed object to the pool and repeat several timing assertions to confirm that the pooled object maintains consistent timing behavior after being returned. During teardown, clear and close the object pool, unregister any remaining MBeans from the management server, verify no pools remain registered, and ensure the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the string substitution functionality of a string substitutor component by testing variable replacement within template strings. Initialize a hash map containing key-value pairs representing template variables, specifically mapping "animal" to "quick brown fox" and "target" to "lazy dog". Clear the builder using the clear method and repeat the testing pattern for String insertion, including boundary validation with invalid indices, null string insertion, and valid string insertion at index 0. Continue this systematic approach for char array insertion, testing with null arrays, empty arrays, and arrays containing characters 'f', 'o', 'o', followed by testing the four-parameter insert method with char arrays, offset, and length parameters, validating boundary conditions for negative indices, out-of-bounds offsets, and invalid lengths. Test primitive data type insertion including boolean values (true and false), char values, int values, long values, float values, and double values, each time clearing the builder, appending "barbaz", validating boundary conditions with assertIndexOutOfBoundsException, and inserting values at index 0 to verify correct string conversion and concatenation. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

Create a second StrBuilder instance and append the string "foo" with start index 0 and length 3 using the append method, then assert that the string representation equals "foo" to confirm basic substring appending functionality. Create a final StrBuilder variable reference and use the assertIndexOutOfBoundsException helper method to verify that calling append with invalid parameter combinations throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, testing scenarios including negative start index with append("bar", -1, 1), start index beyond string length with append("bar", 3, 1), negative length with append("bar", 1, -1), length extending beyond string bounds with append("bar", 1, 3), both negative start index and valid length with append("bar", -1, 3), and start index at string length with positive length append("bar", 4, 0). Verify that appending with valid boundary conditions works correctly by calling append("bar", 3, 0) and asserting the string remains "foo", then append a substring "bar" from the string "abcbardef" starting at index 3 with length 3 and assert the result equals "foobar". Finally, append a CharSequence cast of "abcbardef" starting at index 4 with length 3 and assert the final result equals "foobarard" to test CharSequence parameter handling. The testing framework used is identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the functionality of a single quote character matching utility by verifying that it correctly identifies single quote characters at specific positions within a character buffer. Initialize a single quote matcher using the factory method and confirm that subsequent calls to the same factory method return the identical matcher reference. Create a character buffer containing various characters including a single quote, then test the matcher's ability to detect matches at different positions by calling the matching method with the buffer and specific position indices. Assert that the matcher returns zero when checking positions that do not contain a single quote character, and returns one when checking the position that contains the single quote character, confirming that the matcher correctly identifies single quotes and returns the appropriate match length. The test uses JUnit testing framework.
